questions.q: What is the key difference between an approval and a hold?
options: They are two names for the exact same thing
A hold only applies to invoices, never to orders
An approval routes a decision to a person; a hold is an automatic system stop applied when a condition is met
An approval can never be rejected
questions.explain: Approvals route requests to people for a decision; holds are applied automatically by the system without a human request.

questions.q: What does a credit check typically compare?
options: The order's value (and often the customer's open balance) against their credit limit
The item's weight against the shipping carrier's limit
The order date against the fiscal calendar
The customer's industry against a blocklist
questions.explain: A credit check compares order value, often combined with the customer's current open balance, against their configured credit limit.

questions.q: Why did SO-48217 receive a credit check hold?
options: Harborview Industrial Supply is a brand-new, unverified customer
The ship-to address was invalid
The item was out of stock
Its value, combined with Harborview's existing open balance, failed the automatic credit check at submission
questions.explain: The order's size combined with Harborview's existing open balance caused it to fail the automatic credit check.

questions.q: Who reviewed and released SO-48217's credit check hold?
options: The warehouse shipping clerk
A credit and collections analyst
The customer's own finance team
No one — it released itself automatically after 24 hours
questions.explain: A credit and collections analyst reviewed Harborview's payment history and aging before releasing the hold.

questions.q: Does a credit check hold mean the order is rejected?
options: Yes, a held order is always cancelled
Yes, holds and rejections are identical
No — it is paused and visible for review, not rejected, unless someone decides not to release it
Only if the customer requests cancellation
questions.explain: A hold pauses the order for review; it is not the same as rejecting or cancelling it.
